subject: geography
title: Urbanisation & Megacities
welcome_lead: Trace urban growth from 1950 to today.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on urbanisation trends, megacities and global urban patterns.
final_note: Half of humanity lives in cities; megacities concentrate this growth.

concepts.def: Increase in proportion of population living in towns and cities.
City with population over 10 million; 33 megacities in 2022.
Movement from cities to rural areas, common in MEDCs since 1970s.
Growth of city edges into peri-urban areas.
Return to inner cities, often via regeneration; e.g. London Docklands.
Globally influential centre of finance, culture, ICT; London, NY, Tokyo.

walkthroughs.body_html: 30 percent urban in 1950; 56 percent in 2022; projected 68 percent by 2050 (UN). Asia and Africa drive growth: 90 percent of new urban dwellers between 2018-2050 will live in these regions.

Tokyo (37 million), Delhi (32 million), Shanghai (28 million) lead. Most megacities are now in the Global South. Lagos grew from 1 million (1970) to 21 million (2022). Megacities face housing, transport and infrastructure pressures.

UK is 84 percent urban (2022). Counterurbanisation drove rural population growth in Norfolk and Cornwall. Reurbanisation of London Docklands (Canary Wharf) created 156000 jobs from former dock area. Manchester centre population tripled since 2002.
